_doc: Per-scope step membership for the `gz check` runner (GHI #950). A scope names the steps it DROPS, never the steps it keeps, so a newly registered step is IN every scope until someone deliberately excludes it -- the conservative polarity, matching `overlaps_writers` in data/check_step_concurrency.json. This file exists because the roster was a module-level frozenset in src/gzkit/commands/quality.py, which made 'which steps does the push gate actually run' a code question rather than a declared one. A scope missing from `scopes`, or a missing file, means NO skips: the runner falls back to the full sweep rather than silently dropping steps it could not read a policy for. `records_verified` is the load-bearing field -- a scope that drops any step is a PARTIAL verification, and letting a partial pass record the fingerprint the pre-push gate reuses is precisely the presence-check failure AGENTS.md names ('A PRESENCE CHECK ANSWERS is something armed, NEVER did the governed procedure run'). A scope may record only when it drops nothing the per-change gate runs: `change` (the default, and what the pre-push hook runs) and `full` record (GHI #1088). The `fast` scope was retired 2026-10-11 (GHI #1191), when the `change` scope took its shape: a scope that drops `Test` runs `Test (changed)` in its place.

change.rationale: AMENDED 2026-10-11 (GHI #1191, operator ruling, verbatim: 'I can live with fewer comprehensive checks for daily work with more quality runs at a lesser frequency. I think at minor or patch releases and also as a chore are good places for full qc runs.'): the per-change gate also drops `Test`, `Docs build` and `Guard canary sweep`, and runs `Test (changed)`, the tests the change touches, in place of `Test`. Measured that day on a 10-core host (a dated record): `Test` 117.25s in-gate against 16.34s wall for every remaining step together; the unit tier's wall time was set by one serial test, the 22-mutant canary kill sweep, which is now the full-tier step `Guard canary sweep`. The whole unit tier runs under `gz check --full`, which CI runs on every code push; at OBPI completion (Gate 2, `gz test`); at release (`gz patch release`); and in the `quality-check` chore. What is given up: because work lands on main, a unit failure the changed-test selection misses is reported by CI after the push, and a broken docs link likewise. The sentences below that say this scope keeps the unit tier are the record of 2026-09-24 and are superseded on that point. The DEFAULT scope of plain `gz check` and the scope the pre-push hook runs (GHI #1088). AGENTS.md § Gate Covenant binds the unit tier to every change and `behave` to heavy-lane OBPI work and CI, never to a per-change gate; `gz check --full` is the explicit full sweep, and CI runs it. Until GHI #1088 this was the `prepush` scope, reachable only through `--reuse-verified`, while plain `gz check` was the full sweep and the only scope that could record the reuse fingerprint, so an agent following AGENTS.md § Execution Rules paid Behave on every change to skip a push-gate run that would not have run Behave. It records because it drops nothing the gate that reuses the fingerprint would run. Behave (operator ruling 2026-09-02) is Heavy-lane / closeout-scope by src/gzkit/commands/sync.py's own ruling ('Behave no longer runs as a sync pre-gate ... behave is Heavy-lane / closeout-scope'), but that ruling was applied to git-sync's gate and never reached the `gz check` the pre-push hook calls, so it kept running on every push through the other door. Measured 2026-09-02: 30.61s, the single largest step in the sweep, against 29.10s for Test and 3.90s for Docs build. CI runs the full sweep including Behave (.github/workflows/ci.yml). Removing the step from `gz check` outright was rejected: `Behave` is a declared writer in data/check_step_concurrency.json and is named by test_check_step_writer_overlap.py, test_behave_sharding.py and test_check_step_concurrency.py, so deletion would ripple through the concurrency subsystem to buy the same seconds a scope entry buys here. Preflight (operator ruling 2026-09-02) is a JANITORIAL SCAN, not a correctness gate: it reports stale pipeline markers, orphan receipts and expired locks, and its own output says 'Run with --apply to clean up'. Its verdict is a function of WALL-CLOCK AGE, not of the content being pushed -- `find_stale_pipeline_markers` compares `updated_at` against STALE_MARKER_HOURS=4 -- so it can turn red with no edit at all, and it cannot distinguish a LIVE checkpoint from abandoned residue. Measured instance: OBPI-0.35.0-04 was checkpointed mid-flight with its lock held and `resume_point: verify`, and its two markers then failed Preflight on every commit, locally and in CI, regardless of what was being pushed. A cleanup to-do list must not refuse a push. The full sweep still runs it, so the hygiene signal is not lost -- it simply stops gating.
